title: Your personal AI-check checklist
goal: Assemble a short AI-check card in your own words — five quick checks you'll actually run before trusting any AI output.

blocks.title: Five checks, one card
blocks.body:
You've done the hard part across the last two lessons. Now let's bottle it — into one small card you keep beside your desk.

The five-point AI check:

• Facts — can I confirm each one from a source I trust?
• Level — is it right for my students, not too hard or too easy?
• Bias — does it stereotype, or quietly leave anyone out?
• Source — if it cites something, does that source truly exist and say this?
• Fit — does it suit my class: the board, ₹ and Celsius, familiar examples?

Run these and you're checking like an expert — in under a minute.

options: Can I confirm each fact from a source I trust?
Is there enough here to use?
If it cites a source, does that source actually exist and say this?
Is the source a big, famous name?
Does it fit my class — the board, level, ₹ and Celsius, familiar examples?
Is it written in clear English?

blocks.scaffold: Turn these five checks — facts, level, bias, source, and local fit — into a short, plain-language AI-check card I can keep beside my desk as a {{gradeBand}} {{subject}} teacher. One line per check, phrased as a quick question I ask before trusting any AI output.

blocks.question: How likely are you to actually run this checklist before trusting AI?
